title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: STBench provides unified framework applying benchmarking normalisation methods spatial transcriptomics data. package supports workflow including: quality control; normalisation; spatially variable gene analysis; spatial expression visualisation; gene-set benchmarking; cell-type annotation; spatial clustering; clustering performance evaluation; gene ontology enrichment analysis. vignette demonstrates typical STBench workflow using SpatialExperiment object.

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: development version STBench can installed GitHub. Load package : Depending analyses performed, additional packages may also required.
code: # install.packages("remotes") # remotes::install_github("USERNAME/STBench") library(STBench) library(SpatialExperiment) library(SummarizedExperiment)

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: STBench primarily works SpatialExperiment objects containing count matrix spatial coordinates. vignette, assume object called spe already loaded. object contain raw counts counts assay. computational efficiency experimenting new workflow, users may initially work subset genes spots.
code: spe assayNames(spe) spe <- spe[1:500, 1:2000]

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: Basic quality-control metrics can calculated using add_qc_metrics(). resulting object contains additional QC information can used visualisation filtering.
code: spe_qc <- add_qc_metrics(   spe = spe,   assay_name = "counts",   mito_pattern = "^MT-" )

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: QC distributions can inspected plot_qc(). Individual QC panels can also accessed separately.
code: qc <- plot_qc(   spe = spe_qc,   bins = 45,   show_density = TRUE,   theme_name = "classic" )  qc$plot qc$plots$library_size qc$plots$gene_mean qc$plots$detected_genes qc$plots$mitochondrial

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: Potential filtering thresholds can examined removing observations. Candidate thresholds can supplied directly.
code: cut <- plot_qc_cutoffs(   spe = spe_qc,   library_cutoff = NULL,   gene_cutoff = NULL,   n_points = 200,   theme_name = "classic" )  cut$plot cut_selected <- plot_qc_cutoffs(   spe = spe_qc,   library_cutoff = 2.5,   gene_cutoff = 0.2,   n_points = 200,   theme_name = "classic" )  cut_selected$plot

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: Filtering performed using filter_qc(). QC distributions can reassessed filtering. downstream analyses use filtered object.
code: spe_filtered <- filter_qc(   spe = spe_qc,   library_cutoff = 2.5,   gene_cutoff = 0.01,   recalculate = TRUE,   assay_name = "counts",   mito_pattern = "^MT-" ) qc_after <- plot_qc(   spe = spe_filtered,   bins = 45,   show_density = TRUE,   theme_name = "classic" )  qc_after$plot spe_use <- spe_filtered

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: Multiple normalisation methods can applied common interface using normalize_spe(). output named list containing corresponding normalised SpatialExperiment objects. Additional normalisation methods can included required packages installed.
code: norm <- normalize_spe(   spe = spe_use,   methods = c(     "none",     "scran"   ) )  names(norm)

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: Spatially variable genes can identified using run_svg(). illustration, select small collection genes.
code: svg <- run_svg(   norm_list = norm,   method = "nnSVG",   verbose = TRUE )  names(svg) genes_use <- rownames(spe_use)[1:5]

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: SVG statistics can compared across normalisation methods.
code: svg_stat <- plot_svg_stat(   svg_norm = svg,   genes = genes_use,   stat = "LR_stat",   transform = "log" )  svg_stat$plot

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: corresponding SVG ranks can also visualised.
code: svg_rank <- plot_svg_rank(   svg,   genes = genes_use )  svg_rank$plot

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: Spatial expression patterns can compared across normalisation methods using plot_spatial_expression().

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: Expression values can scaled facilitate comparison spatial patterns.
code: p_scaled <- plot_spatial_expression(   norm_list = norm,   genes = genes_use,   assay_name = "logcounts",   scale_expr = TRUE,   point_size = 0.5,   colour_option = "magma",   theme_name = "classic" )  p_scaled$plot

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: Original normalised expression values can also displayed.
code: p_original <- plot_spatial_expression(   norm_list = norm,   genes = genes_use,   assay_name = "logcounts",   scale_expr = FALSE,   point_size = 0.5,   colour_option = "magma",   ncol_genes = 1,   theme_name = "classic" )  p_original$plot

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: Known gene sets can used evaluate different normalisation methods affect SVG detection.

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: example, set housekeeping stable genes can examined.
code: stable <- plot_svg_gene_set_distribution(   svg,   genes = Housekeeping_Genes$Gene.name,   stat = "LR_stat",   transform = "log",   plot_type = "boxplot" )  stable$plot

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: proportion genes selected gene set among highest-ranked SVGs can also calculated.
code: topn <- plot_svg_topn_gene_set(   svg_list = svg,   genes = Housekeeping_Genes$Gene.name,   top_n = c(     10,     20,     50,     100   ) )  topn$plot

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: Cell-type annotation can performed normalisation method using run_annotation(). suitable reference dataset corresponding cell-type labels must first provided.
code: annotation_results <- run_annotation(   norm_list = norm,   ref = ref,   labels = ref$cell_type_spec,   de.method = "wilcox" )

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
code: p_annotation <- plot_spatial_annotation(   annotation_list = annotation_results,   label_col = "SingleR_label",   ncol = 2 )  p_annotation$plot

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
code: p_celltype <- plot_celltype_proportion(   annotation_list = annotation_results,   label_col = "SingleR_label" )  p_celltype$plot

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: Agreement cell-type assignments across normalisation methods can assessed using:
code: p_agree <- plot_annotation_agreement(   norm_list = annotation_results,   annotation_col = "SingleR_label" )  p_agree$plot

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: STBench provides interface running BANKSY independently normalisation method. Cluster assignments can inspected directly.
code: banksy_norm <- run_banksy_individual(   norm_list = norm,   cluster_col = "banksy_cluster",   k_geom = 15,   lambda = 0.8,   resolution = 0.2,   seed = 123 ) table(banksy_norm$none$banksy_cluster) table(banksy_norm$scran$banksy_cluster)

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
code: cluster_plot <- plot_spatial_clustering(   norm_list = banksy_norm,   cluster_col = "banksy_cluster",   method_order = c(     "none",     "scran"   ),   point_size = 0.5 )  cluster_plot$plot

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: ground-truth biological labels available, clustering performance can quantified using Adjusted Rand Index (ARI).

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
code: ari_results <- calculate_ari(   norm_list = banksy_norm,   ground_truth_col = "layer_guess",   cluster_col = "banksy_cluster" )  ari_results

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: Higher ARI values indicate greater agreement inferred spatial clusters supplied reference labels.
code: ari_plot <- plot_ari(   ari_df = ari_results,   method_order = c(     "none",     "scran"   ) )  ari_plot$plot

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: Cluster-specific marker genes can identified used downstream Gene Ontology enrichment analysis. appropriate organism annotation package must supplied OrgDb.
code: go_results <- calculate_go(   norm_list = banksy_norm,   cluster_col = "banksy_cluster",   methods = c(     "none",     "scran"   ),   OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.eg.db )

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: top marker genes used enrichment analysis can visualised :
code: go_genes_plot <- plot_go_genes(   go_results = go_results,   top_n = 5,   method_order = c(     "none",     "scran"   ) )  go_genes_plot$plot

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
code: go_plot <- plot_go(   go_results = go_results,   top_n = 5,   method_order = c(     "none",     "scran"   ) )  go_plot$plot

title: STBench: Benchmarking Normalisation Methods for Spatial Transcriptomics
text: STBench provides consistent workflow comparing normalisation methods across several downstream spatial transcriptomics analyses. typical analysis consists : performing quality control; applying one normalisation methods; detecting spatially variable genes; examining spatial expression patterns; benchmarking predefined gene sets; evaluating cell-type annotations; performing spatial clustering; comparing clustering accuracy; assessing cluster-specific biological enrichment. framework allows results different normalisation approaches generated compared using common interface.
